Validate a Data Frame Against a Provenance Schema

Source: R/lib_data_loader.R
valsch.Rd

Checks a data frame against the schema block of a provenance record: required columns, row-count bounds, column types, numeric ranges, missingness and allowed category values. It returns the problems it finds instead of stopping, so the caller can log them, show them, or pass the same schema to schval(), the wrapper that turns them into errors and warnings. Use it each time a file is re-downloaded, to catch a re-release that renamed, retyped or recoded a column.

Usage

valsch(dfraw, prov)

Arguments

dfraw

The data frame to validate.

prov

A provenance list as returned by loadprov(), or list(schema = infsch(df)). The schema block may contain:

  • expected_columns – required column names (character). A missing one is "fatal"; everything else below is a "warning".

  • structural_invariants – a list with min_data_rows and max_data_rows (numbers of rows).

  • expected_value_sets – a named list of allowed values per column.

  • expected_types – a named character vector of expected classes. integer, numeric and double are treated as interchangeable, since a re-release legitimately widens one to another.

  • numeric_ranges – a named list of c(min =, max =) bounds.

  • max_missing_fraction – a named numeric of per-column ceilings on the share of NA, between 0 and 1.

infsch() produces all six from data you already trust.

Value

A named list of issues; each issue is a list with severity ("fatal" or "warning") and a human-readable message. The names are those listed in Details. A zero-length list means the data frame is clean.

Details

Every schema field is optional and is checked only when present, so a schema written for an earlier version keeps working unchanged.

This is the STRUCTURAL check – names, types, bounds, value sets. It cannot tell you that a column kept its name, type and range while its distribution moved; cpsdrft() answers that. Rules that are particular to a data set (an age must be non-negative, two dates must be ordered) belong in rul() and valrules().

The checks, and the name of the issue each one adds:

  • a missing expected_columns entry: missing_columns, "fatal";

  • fewer than min_data_rows or more than max_data_rows rows: row_count_low / row_count_high;

  • a column whose class differs from expected_types: type_<col>. integer, numeric and double are one family, and so are character and factor;

  • non-missing values outside numeric_ranges (inclusive bounds; non-numeric columns are skipped): range_<col>;

  • a share of NA above max_missing_fraction: missing_<col>;

  • values not in expected_value_sets: unexpected_<col>.

A column named in a check but absent from the data is skipped by that check (only expected_columns reports it). All of these are "warning" except missing_columns.

The schema itself is checked too. An empty schema (list()) gives one schema_empty warning. An unknown field name within three edits of a known one (expected_colums) is "fatal", because it would otherwise be ignored silently; any other unknown name is a warning. An unknown structural invariant one edit, or one swap of neighbouring letters, away from min_data_rows or max_data_rows is fatal; other invariant names are left alone. expected_dtypes is accepted as another name for expected_types, and synthetic_recipe is a known field that is not checked here.

Errors: dfraw that is not a data frame; a schema that is not a list. A prov that is NULL or has no schema returns an empty list (use schval() to make that an error).

See also

infsch() to derive a schema, cpsdrft() for the distributional check, schval() to raise on the issues.

Examples

prov <- list(schema = list(
  expected_columns      = c("id", "year"),
  structural_invariants = list(min_data_rows = 1),
  expected_value_sets   = list(year = 2020:2025)
))
df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, year = c(2020, 2021, 2030))
issues <- valsch(df, prov)
names(issues) # flags the out-of-set year value
#> [1] "unexpected_year"

# A column that silently changed type is caught.
typed <- list(schema = list(expected_types = c(id = "integer")))
valsch(data.frame(id = c("1", "2")), typed)[[1]]$message
#> [1] "Column 'id' is character, expected integer"

# So is a value outside its pinned range, and excess missingness.
ranged <- list(schema = list(numeric_ranges = list(v = c(min = 0, max = 1))))
valsch(data.frame(v = c(0.5, 9)), ranged)[[1]]$message
#> [1] "Column 'v' has 1 value(s) outside [0, 1]"

gappy <- list(schema = list(max_missing_fraction = c(v = 0.1)))
valsch(data.frame(v = c(1, NA, NA, 4)), gappy)[[1]]$message
#> [1] "Column 'v' is 50.0% missing, above the expected 10.0%"

# A clean frame produces nothing.
length(valsch(data.frame(id = 1:3, year = 2021), prov))
#> [1] 0

# a misspelt schema field is fatal rather than silently ignored
valsch(df, list(schema = list(expcol = "id")))[[1]]
#> $severity
#> [1] "warning"
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "schema field 'expcol' is not one valsch() uses: it was not checked"
#> 

# a schema inferred from trusted data, checked against a new release
sch <- infsch(data.frame(id = 1:3, year = 2020:2022))
names(valsch(data.frame(id = 1:2), list(schema = sch)))
#> [1] "missing_columns"

# the data must be a data frame
try(valsch(list(id = 1), prov))
#> Error : `dfraw` must be a data frame
